title: I miss gore animations like in first Fallout, so I am implementing them to my game
author: LegendaryJohnny
selftext:
I really don't understand why more games does not have limbs dismemberment and gore effects looking like this? I was always thinking it must be due to difficulty of develop such a system but nope, Claude gets it in 1 minute.

In first 2 Fallouts there were so many creative finisher animations. Then maybe Soldier of Fortune, Kingpin, Mortal Kombat obviously, newer Fallouts were trying to do that but it was too repetetive and looked lame. And thats about it. So yeah, my dream game WILL have it :D

comments.author: Gestaltarskiten
comments.body: Simple. Because of a wider audience if you can sell to younger people. Thats it.

replies.author: XeniaJP
replies.body: Like that is stopping billions of literal children in a month playing GTA 6

comments.author: KeenAsGreen
comments.body:
Dismemberment is almost an instant r18+.
Most studios dont want that

replies.author: LegendaryJohnny
replies.body: Which I really dont care, I want game with animations like attached. That is why I am creating game for MYSELF in the first place :D

replies.author: KeenAsGreen
replies.body: Totally agree. I have a fun little game im working on with full gore including dismemberment and gibs.

replies.author: LegendaryJohnny
replies.body:
hope you will share. I feel like in 1 or 2 years we will get really good and creative games thanks to AI. yeah now almost everything is "slop" because its new. I am working on this already dozen of hours, just element after element to see how to sort things out. When every element is in place, I will start building the game with all systems working. I already built level editor with claude, so I can create all levels manually and I created very decent area looking like my childhood neighbourhood. Still need to create dozens of 3D models for that map though and handcraft all roads and sidewalks not to look too uniformed. But I already also have interactive snow which I can add freely on the map. So map design is pretty much sorted at this point.

Now I will create turn based fight system with those gore animations applied. Probably inventory and weapon selections as well. This will be work for another dozens of hours I feel. Then I will add skill system and character creation. Then I will add dialogues and quest system, maybe with minimap. Then I have to create variety of enemies and animate them, NPCs and questlines. Then more music, having just 2 songs (from tool I created earlier with Claude). Then I will have first map out of many for my game - which will be just demo basically. And all of this is at least year of working after 9 to 5. Then nobody will play it only me lol. So yeah. You can create decent games with AI, but not with 1 prompt.

You can check their conference talk here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=98j3XacsocQ

replies.author: LegendaryJohnny
replies.body:
Oh yeah I am playing it on my Rog Ally here and there. Got it for free on Epic. Its satisfying to smash zombies with fire axe and body deformation is good. But it is in same rank as Fallout 3 or 4. I miss variations and creativity. Maybe finishers from Doom 2016, Eternal, Dark Ages are great. The issue is you fight zombies or monsters in action gam, so hectoliters of blood are kinda expected.

Its not as satisfying as doing critical in Fallout 2 and make a big hole in a body of human raider with your Gauss Gun tho 🤣

Thinking about it I completely forgot about TLOU2 where the gore was amazingly done and killing a bandit with booby trap was extremely satisfying. So its not like we are completely without it in games, but it is definitely missing in RPG genre.
